comments.author: jjackson
comments.body:
## Correction to this issue's evidence: the cache is NOT ruled out

Third consecutive session on the same halt (`spark-facilitator`, pre-flight Step 2a, plugin 0.13.1060, claude pid 76129, Claude Code 2.1.248). This one has a timing measurement the prior two did not, and it contradicts one line in the body above.

The body states:

> needs-auth cache auto-cleared this session (`cleared: true`) and the symptom persisted, so the cache is definitively not the cause

That inference does not hold, because **the clear happens inside the session it is meant to fix, after nova has already bound.** Measured timeline:

```
17:45:23  previous session writes handoff (its doctor had already cleared the nova cache entry)
17:45:51  THIS session's claude process starts (pid 76129)          <-- nova binds HERE
17:46:19  this session's doctor finds plugin:nova:nova in the cache
          again and clears it (cleared: true)                        <-- 28s too late
```

Commands:

```
$ ps -o pid,lstart -p 76129
76129 Thu Aug 27 17:45:51 2026

$ stat -f '%Sm' ~/.claude/mcp-needs-auth-cache.json
Aug 27 17:46:19 2026

$ stat -f '%Sm' ~/.ace/session-handoff.json
Aug 27 17:45:23 2026
```

So `cleared: true` is *expected* whether or not the cache is the cause — it only tells you the entry was present 28 seconds into the session. A too-late clear and a non-causal cache produce identical `cleared: true` output, which is why this reading cannot discriminate between them.

## The fact that is actually new

The entry is being **re-added at or immediately after every session start**. The previous session cleared it; 28 seconds later, in a fresh process, it was back. The clear has never once survived a session boundary — so no session has yet *started* with the cache clean, and the remedy has never actually been tested under the condition it needs.

## What I could NOT determine, stated plainly

I cannot tell from inside this session whether nova was in the cache **at** 17:45:51 (cause: stale entry short-circuits the `headersHelper` PAT path) or was added **between** 17:45:51 and 17:46:19 by this session's own failed connection (symptom: PAT genuinely fails, cache is downstream). Both fit the data. I did not want to assert either, having just corrected an assertion.

## The experiment that discriminates, and its decision rule

The cache is clear **right now** — a state no session boundary has seen. So the next restart is a real test rather than a repeat:

1. Cmd-Q + reopen. Do **not** run `Clear authentication` again; do **not** call `authenticate`.
2. **Before** running `bin/ace-doctor` — the doctor clears the entry and destroys the evidence — run `cat ~/.claude/mcp-needs-auth-cache.json`.
3. `ToolSearch select:mcp__plugin_nova_nova__get_hq_connection,mcp__plugin_nova_nova__list_projects`

| Outcome | Reading | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **A** — atoms resolve | cache staleness was the cause; the clear simply never survived a boundary | fix is to clear **before/at** connection, not mid-session; correct the body line above |
| **B** — still auth-only, **and** a fresh `plugin:nova:nova` entry timestamped at that session's start | the PAT genuinely fails at connection with the OAuth token already gone | this is the escalation — stop restarting, escalate with the fresh timestamp |

## Suggested scope change

The correlation fix described in the body (route the remediation branch off the handoff) is still right and still worth doing. But it routes between *two remedies that have both now failed*. The ordering defect is the more expensive one: `bin/ace-doctor`'s auto-clear (#1579) can only ever help the next session, while its `remediation` text reads as though it helped this one. Whatever the outcome of the experiment above, the auto-clear should either run somewhere that precedes connection or say explicitly that it takes effect on the **next** start.

Written from a run that halted correctly at the fence with no run folder created; full context in `~/.ace/session-handoff.json`.

comments.author: jjackson
comments.body:
Hit this loop again today on a different machine (user `acedimagi`, Claude Code **2.1.250**, ACE 0.13.1060). Adding the measurement because the missing piece is **deterministically checkable** and no current probe checks it.

## The condition that actually causes the loop

ace#1629 identified the mechanism (2.1.238 changed the env passed to `headersHelper`; nova's helper is env-var dependent). What no probe asserts is the *observable consequence*:

```
$ ps -Eww -p <claude-pid> | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -c '^NOVA_API_KEY='
0
$ ps -Eww -p <claude-pid> | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -cE '^[A-Z_]+='
25          # <-- control: env IS visible, so the 0 above is real, not SIP
```

Simulating nova's helper under that env:

```
/bin/sh   -> {}
/bin/zsh  -> {"Authorization":"Bearer <redacted>"}
```

`/bin/sh` does not read `.zshenv`, which is where `~/.ace/env.sh` gets sourced. So the helper emits `{}`, no Authorization header is sent, and Claude Code falls back to OAuth — whose token lacks `nova.hq.read`.

## Why "Clear authentication" cannot break the loop

This is the part worth writing down. `Clear authentication` removes the OAuth token, but with `NOVA_API_KEY` absent from the process env there is **no PAT to fall back to** — the helper still returns `{}`. So the session immediately re-prompts OAuth and re-writes `plugin:nova:nova` into `mcp-needs-auth-cache.json`. The operator restarts, and lands in the same state.

The current remediation strings route a recurrence to `/mcp -> Clear authentication` as the terminal answer. On 2.1.238+ that step is a no-op by construction, so the operator loops on the *documented* fix. Observed here: many restarts, no progress.

## Ancestry matters

```
launchd -> Emdash.app -> Emdash Helper -> claude
```

Emdash's own process env has 14 vars and no `NOVA_API_KEY` (GUI/Finder launch). Every claude it spawns inherits that. A claude launched from a shell would have the key — which is why this reproduces on one machine and not another with byte-identical config (same `.mcp.json`, same `.zshenv`, no `env` block in either `settings.json`).

## Suggested probe

A no-network check that beats every existing one, because it tests the consequence rather than the cause:

1. read the claude pid's env (with the `grep -cE '^[A-Z_]+='` control so an unreadable env is reported as `skip`, never `pass`)
2. if `NOVA_API_KEY` is absent -> the helper WILL emit `{}` -> report `fail` with the ace#1629 static-header remedy, **not** the Clear-authentication remedy

`nova_shell_env` today checks the *shell* env (which has the key via `.zshenv`) and passes — it is measuring the wrong process. That is why this machine reported `nova_needs_auth_cache: pass` / `nova_shell_env: PASS` while nova was completely unauthenticated.

## Resolution here

Reinstalled the ace#1629 workaround:

```
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user nova https://mcp.commcare.app/mcp --header 'Authorization: Bearer <PAT>'
```

Worth noting it was **not** present on either mac user, including one where nova had previously been working — so the workaround is being lost (plugin reinstall / config reset / manual cleanup following the `nova_shell_env` WARN that ace#1629 flagged as harmful). While voidcraft-labs/nova-plugin#52 is open, this config is load-bearing and something keeps removing it.

comments.author: jjackson
comments.body:
## Re-validation: the heal fired on a second machine, and the probe now PASSes

Routed here from a canopy `agent-review ace --hours 24` finding ("Nova `scope_missing`
failures survive session restarts with no escalation path"), which cited three sessions.
Re-validating against `origin/main @ c1ced4ad` puts all three **before** the fix, so the
finding is a restatement of this issue rather than new evidence — recording the timeline
and one live reading, since neither was on the issue yet.

### The three cited sessions all predate 784d484f

```
$ git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=iso -- lib/nova-header-readiness.ts
784d484f 2026-08-28 07:12:26 -0600  fix(doctor): measure whether Nova will actually
                                    receive an auth header, and self-heal (#1769)

$ for s in acdfe787 58473417 2248f3f0; do stat -f '%Sm' -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M' \
    $(find ~/.claude/projects -name "${s}*.jsonl"); done
2026-08-28 09:46      # acdfe787 — worktree emdash-bednet-7g9p6
2026-08-27 17:37      # 58473417
2026-08-27 17:36      # 2248f3f0
```

The two 08-27 sessions precede the merge by ~14h. `acdfe787` postdates it only because
it is the session that *did the work* — it lives in `emdash-bednet-7g9p6`, the branch
merged as PR #1772 carrying 784d484f. Its `human_corrections[0]` ("tried many times to
restart sessions", "not working") is this issue's problem statement, not an
unaddressed recurrence.

### Live reading on `acedimagi` after the heal

```
$ npx tsx scripts/doctor-nova-header.ts --format=lines
PASS nova_header_readiness: user-scope nova entry carries a static Authorization header
(voidcraft-labs/nova-plugin#52 workaround active) — the headersHelper is bypassed
```

Run WITHOUT `--heal`, so this is reading state a prior `--heal` installed, not creating
it. This is the machine whose measurement is in the 2026-08-28T12:18Z comment above
(`grep -c '^NOVA_API_KEY=' → 0` against 25 env-var control). Same machine, override now
present and asserted — so the self-heal survived a session boundary here, which is the
condition that comment noted had never actually been tested.

### The suggestion I was routed to ship, and why I did not

The proposal was a runtime rail: halt nova calls on the first `scope_missing` response
and surface a fixed re-auth message. Two reasons that is the wrong shape now:

1. A hook cannot see it. ACE's only PreToolUse hook fires **pre-call** and receives the
   tool input, never the MCP response, so a rail written there cannot observe
   `scope_missing` at all. It would need a PostToolUse detector plus a PreToolUse
   sentinel — two hooks — to reproduce what preflight already does in one static check.
2. Reacting to the Nth failed response is strictly worse than the layer that shipped.
   `nova_header_readiness` answers the same question *before any nova call is made*,
   and heals it. `agents/ace-orchestrator.md:109` ranks it above `nova_needs_auth_cache`
   and says to ignore the cache remedy when it fails.

### What I could NOT determine

Whether a stored OAuth credential outranks the **static header** the way #52 says it
outranks the `headersHelper` PAT. If it does, a session could read
`nova_header_readiness: pass` and `nova_needs_auth_cache: fail` together — and the cache
block at `bin/ace-doctor:397` still leads with the "FIRST occurrence: Cmd-Q + reopen"
branch, which is the exact defect this issue was filed for. `scripts/doctor-nova-header.ts`
does not reason about precedence (`grep -n -i 'outrank\|oauth'` → zero hits), so I have
no basis to claim it either way and did not want to assert one. That is the residual
worth closing or ruling out before this issue does.

comments.body:
## Follow-up shipped: PR #1791 — the terminal remedy itself was wrong

Chasing the residual I flagged in my previous comment ("does stored OAuth outrank the
**static** header?") answered it, and turned up something worse than the residual.

**The answer is no — because stored-OAuth precedence was never real.** Your own third
correction on voidcraft-labs/nova-plugin#52 (2026-08-25) disproved it with the client
logs:

```
Successfully retrieved 0 headers from headersHelper
No access token in storage
```

No stored token, so nothing to outrank. And `lib/nova-header-readiness.ts:142` already
says the static header "outranks every other credential path."

**What that exposed.** Four operator-facing surfaces still carried the disproved
mechanism and terminated at `/mcp` → `Clear authentication`:

```
$ grep -rn "outrank" agents/ playbook/ bin/ace-doctor      # before #1791
agents/commcare-setup.md:206      "cause is a stored OAuth token outranking"
agents/ace-orchestrator.md:328    same
bin/ace-doctor:381,397,399,2527   same, in two live remediation strings
```

So this issue's complaint held one layer deeper than filed: it is not only that nothing
*selects* between the branches — the branch the operator is finally routed to is itself
a no-op by construction. `lib/nova-header-readiness.ts` (merged 07:12 today) had the
mechanism right; the prose lagged it by three days.

`agents/ace-orchestrator.md` also had the `ps -Eww` premise inverted — it read a
*present* `NOVA_API_KEY` as the diagnosis, when **absence** is the tell on 2.1.238+.

**Shipped in #1791** (merged, v0.13.1069): cause re-attributed to the header mechanism in
all four surfaces, remedy re-pointed at the static-header override that
`nova_header_readiness --heal` installs, playbook forensics kept under a `MECHANISM
CORRECTED` banner, plus `test/agents/nova-remediation-currency.test.ts` — verified to
FAIL on each file's pre-fix content, not merely pass on the new.

A test rather than a note because `scripts/probe-upstream-asks.ts` is structurally blind
here: nova-plugin#52 is still **OPEN**, and the mechanism was corrected *in a comment*.
The probe reports issues ACE cites as live that have CLOSED — a corrected-but-open issue
trips nothing.

**Leaving this issue open, deliberately.** #1791 removes the operator harm by a different
route than the fix this issue specifies. Your literal ask — correlating the handoff block
with the nova cache block in `bin/ace-doctor` so the recurrence branch is *selected*
rather than left to the reader — is still unimplemented. Whether that is still worth
building now that `nova_header_readiness` outranks the cache block and self-heals is your
call, not mine.
